section: Closing strips and fillers for Maxima and Intarsio
source_pages: printed p.434 / PDF 436 (the H.198 row of the first position)
family_note: NO FAMILY-LEVEL KEYS. A filler takes its height, its ground and its plinth from the family it joins - see fillers_h78.json, which states the reasoning once for all of these files. Extracted only because family Tall H.198 already exists in this registry: a filler extracted ahead of its family would silently inherit Standards defaults instead of its own ground.

filler_front.description: Filler in door finishes from 2,3 to 15 cm - front in door finishes

front_layout.note: One finished front covering the whole face. NO hinge_axis and no mechanism - A FILLER DOES NOT OPEN, so 70_symbols draws no leaf, which is the same treatment a US appliance panel gets: it too states a single front it never swings. The kind is STATED rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs and Panel.gola_options both default a missing layout to 'single', and a default is not a source. THIS FAMILY DECLARES NO DOOR-VERSION AXIS, so nothing about this front changes with a gola run and no front height from another family may be written here.

filler_front.notes: Row H.198 of the twelve-row table. The prefix is the height-family letter, the same lookup the unit chapters use. THE SUFFIX IS NOT DECODABLE ACROSS PREFIXES: 0151 here is a front-only strip, while 0151 on a P prefix is a wall filler WITH a one-piece bottom. Read the table, not the digits. Width is not in the code - one article covers 23 to 150 mm and the width is stated per order. DEPTH 22 RECORDED 2026-08-24, AND IT IS A DECISION WITH A SOURCE, NOT A PRINTED DIMENSION AGAINST THIS CODE. Until today this article was held buildable:false because printed p.434 prints no depth beside its table and the 2,2 stated all over the catalog was, correctly, refused as a guess (learned rule 8). What changed is that the PAGE WAS LOOKED AT rather than read. Three things carry it: (1) THE SECTION DETAIL OF THIS POSITION, rendered at 300 dpi, draws the strip as a SINGLE LAYER standing in the front plane, fixed to the hatched neighbouring carcass by an ANGLE BRACKET - there is no box behind it and no depth to choose; and the foot beneath it is drawn DASHED, so the article ends at the front line and the plinth zone belongs to the run and not to the strip. (2) THE POSITION DIRECTLY BELOW IT ON THE SAME PAGE - the same 'front in door finishes' on a melamine box - carries a DIMENSIONED detail: 35 / 0,3 / 2,2, that is box 350 + gap 3 + front 22. The front thickness of this page is therefore printed, one position over, on the same article family. (3) Independently, Cesar's own SketchUp export of estimate 2026/30831 measures FRONT_T_MM = 22 (_manifest.json factory_confirmations, trust CONFIRMED). Andriy's decision, 2026-08-24, recorded under learned rule 4. If Elda contradicts it this is a DATA change and not a code change. ATTACHED, NOT STANDING. printed p.434 draws the bracket; the engine does not draw it and does not need to. What the drawing settles for us is the two things that matter: the panel is COPLANAR with the fronts beside it, and it BEGINS at the neighbouring front line - which is its own family's plinth height, declared per family and never global. Below that line is the plinth, which is a RUN item ordered by the linear metre (printed p.625: front plinth ZOCC001 at H.6 and ZOCC011 at H.10, the only two heights the catalog sells) and which may be absent entirely. So the strip is drawn from the family's plinth top to the family's front height, and nothing about the plinth is implied by the article.
